items.title: 52240_Frank _Machito_ Grillo oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Who asked you to record 'Cubop City' or asked you to do it again, was it Morris Levy or Teddy Reig? [INTERVIEWEE] Teddy Reig.

ctx.x: Teddy Reig. Teddy Reig was a jitterbug dancer since nineteen, since opened, the Savoy was opened. He used to go up there every night, so he was jazz-inclined all his life, so he had an idea, almost perfect idea, who played good jazz. So that was a good combination between Teddy Reig, Symphony Sid, a good radio disk jockey. He know what he was talking about. He know about that particular music, very well; so Brew Moore was coming up, a young musician, with good ideas, and Howard McGhee was already established. So…

And they happened to be lucky they was very flexible too, because almost was a contradiction to put a tenor-sax and a trumpet player playing against our rhythm that is so complicated. Is complicated for the people that play. (chuckle)
